narr: Two rounds of thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast California, one round during the very early morning hours, between midnight through 4 am local time and another round during the mid to late afternoon hours. The early morning round was instigated by outflow boundaries that moved westward into southeast California from the decaying storm complex across southwest Arizona during the evening hours on the 12th. The environment was characterized by high moisture content (PWATs in excess of 2 inches) and moderate instability (MLCAPE of around 1000 J/KG). The mid to late afternoon round, was a more typical diurnal instigator and the environment once again was conducive, with very high moisture content (PWATs of 2+inches) and high instability (MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/KG).
ev: Highway 78 was flooded at Milpitas Wash with debris across the road. A vehicle was reported to have been damaged by the rocks on the road. No injuries were reported.
Ogilby Road closed near the intersection with Sidewinder Road due to flooding. Vehicles were stranded between two washes pushing sediment and debris onto roadways. No injuries were reported.
SR-177, just north of Desert Center, was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Highway 78 near Milepost 53 was flooded, with multiple vehicles stuck in the floodwaters. No damages or injuries were reported.
